key_insight: UniD shows that a single video model can learn to predict many dense scene properties at once from disjoint datasets, without needing every training sample to have all labels. It reduces the reliance on expensive pseudo-labeling and makes unified scene understanding more practical.
problem_solved: The paper addresses the fragmentation of dense video annotations across incompatible datasets, which makes it hard to train one model for depth, normals, semantics, and other scene properties together.
method: Introduces UniD, a unified video model that jointly predicts eight dense scene properties from video.
Trains on disjoint data sources instead of requiring fully co-annotated datasets, enabling broader supervision.
Avoids heavy pseudo-labeling pipelines by learning a shared representation across tasks and datasets.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this means unified multi-task scene understanding can be trained more efficiently and flexibly using existing datasets. It lowers annotation and compute barriers for building richer perception systems.

paper_title: Unified Video Dense Prediction from Disjoint Data
paper_authors: Yihong Sun, Seoung Wug Oh, Jiahui Huang, Bharath Hariharan, Joon-Young Lee
